request.input:
Bill number: HB2356
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 2258
 By Taylor

 HOUSE BILL 2356

 By Howell

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Section
 55-8-151, relative to evidence.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 55-8-151(c)(2), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting instead the following:

 (A) An LEA that installs cameras on the exterior of school buses in accordance

 with subdivision (c)(1) shall enter into a memorandum of understanding with local law

 enforcement that includes, but is not limited to, the review of evidence from a camera

 and overall enforcement. Unless otherwise authorized by law, only POST-certified or

 state-commissioned law enforcement officers, including school resource officers, as

 defined in § 49-6-4202, are authorized to review evidence from a camera to determine

 whether a violation of subdivision (a)(1) has occurred.

 (B) In addition to, and not in limitation of, the memorandum of understanding

 required in subdivision (c)(2)(A), an LEA may authorize school security personnel to

 review evidence from a camera to determine whether a violation of subdivision (a)(1)

 has occurred. The use of school safety personnel under this subdivision (c)(2)(B) does

 not prohibit or restrict an LEA from entering into or maintaining a memorandum of

 understanding with a law enforcement agency under subdivision (c)(2)(A), and both

 review processes may be used concurrently. For purposes of this subdivision (c)(2)(B),

 "school safety personnel" means a school safety officer, school resource officer, or other

 individual employed or contracted by an LEA whose duties include student safety or

 campus security.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would change who may review evidence from cameras installed on the outside of school buses to determine whether a violation of Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 55-8-151(a)(1), occurred. An LEA that installs the cameras must have an agreement with local law enforcement covering evidence review and overall enforcement. Unless otherwise authorized by law, only POST-certified or state-commissioned law enforcement officers, including school resource officers, may review the evidence. The bill also permits an LEA to authorize school security personnel to review it. It defines “school safety personnel” for this provision as school safety officers, school resource officers, and other LEA employees or contractors whose duties include student safety or campus security. The LEA may use both review processes at the same time. The bill would take effect upon becoming law.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA that installs the cameras must have an agreement with local law enforcement covering evidence review and overall enforcement.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the mandatory agreement, responsible LEA, local law enforcement counterpart, and both required subjects. The preceding sentence identifies exterior school-bus cameras.

assessments.summary_quote: Unless otherwise authorized by law, only POST-certified or state-commissioned law enforcement officers, including school resource officers, may review the evidence.
assessments.rationale: Preserves the legal exception, exclusive officer qualifications, and inclusion of school resource officers. The opening sentence identifies the evidence-review purpose and relevant violation.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill also permits an LEA to authorize school security personnel to review it.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the LEA's discretionary authorization of school security personnel to review the same evidence for violations. The mandatory agreement and concurrent-review statements establish that this authority supplements rather than replaces the agreement.

assessments.summary_quote: The LEA may use both review processes at the same time.
assessments.rationale: Expressly conveys concurrent review. Together with the mandatory law-enforcement agreement, this communicates that using school personnel does not displace that agreement.

assessments.summary_quote: It defines “school safety personnel” for this provision as school safety officers, school resource officers, and other LEA employees or contractors whose duties include student safety or campus security.
assessments.rationale: Includes all defined personnel categories, the employment or contracting relationship, the qualifying duties, and the definition's limited application.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would take effect upon becoming law.
